usageNotes: Use this to reset or set an OS-level user password inside a running QEMU VM without needing SSH access or console login. Requires the QEMU Guest Agent to be installed, running, and responsive inside the guest — the call will fail with a timeout error if the agent is not active. The caller must hold the VM.GuestAgent.Unrestricted privilege on /vms/{vmid}; this is intentionally a high-trust permission because it allows password takeover of any guest OS account.

examples.summary: Reset the 'administrator' password on a Windows VM (VMID 201) running on node 'pve1'

tips: The QEMU Guest Agent must be installed inside the guest (qemu-guest-agent package on Linux, VirtIO drivers on Windows) and the agent service must be running before this call will succeed.
Passwords are transmitted to the Proxmox API over HTTPS and then passed to the guest agent over the virtio-serial channel — they do not traverse the network inside the guest.
Set 'crypted: true' only when passing a pre-hashed password string (e.g., output of crypt(3)); most callers should leave it false and pass the plaintext password.
This endpoint does not return a UPID — it is synchronous and returns immediately once the guest agent confirms the change.

On Linux guests, this uses the guest agent's guest-set-user-password command, which internally calls the passwd utility or equivalent; password complexity rules enforced by the guest OS still apply and may cause the call to fail silently or return an error.
